headings.title: Connect with a Gmail app password

html:
Gmail Integration

smTO is not an email client. Gmail is the source of truth. smTO does not maintain a mailbox copy, inbox index, message/thread cache, draft mirror, label cache, or background synchronization database. Searches and reads query Gmail when requested.

Connect with a Gmail app password

In Parameter Store → New parameter template, select Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP). Save the following JSON as personal_gmail, replacing the email and password:

{
  "profile_type": "gmail_app_password_account",
  "profile_version": 1,
  "email": "you@gmail.com",
  "app_password": "YOUR_GOOGLE_APP_PASSWORD",
  "display_name": "",
  "timeout_seconds": 30
}

Use a Google app password, not your normal Google password. Google requires 2-Step Verification; account or administrator policies can make app passwords unavailable. Follow Google's app-password setup. Only leading and trailing spaces in app passwords are trimmed when saving; internal spaces are preserved. Google-hosted custom-domain addresses work with this profile too. No OAuth application, consent screen, or callback is needed. Saved accounts are configured; saving performs no network request.

The selected paired Gateway needs this release's gmail_imap v1 and email_smtp support plus Gmail workflow capability version 1 for compound actions. Update and restart both the controller and selected Gateway to deploy these actions. Older Gateways report gmail_gateway_upgrade_required before a new workflow writes mail. Connections use verified TLS to imap.gmail.com:993 and verified STARTTLS to smtp.gmail.com:587. The profile does not accept custom hosts or insecure TLS. Update older Gateways if the private Gmail operation route is unavailable.

Example prompts:

  • “Test Gmail IMAP and SMTP with @personal_gmail.”
  • “Use Gmail with @personal_gmail to summarize unread messages from today.”
  • “Use Email / SMTP with @personal_gmail to send this message to alice@example.com.”

gmail.test_connection(account_ref="@personal_gmail") tests both connections independently without changing mail or sending anything. email.test_connection(profile_key="@personal_gmail") tests SMTP only. Both skills use this one saved record. Enable each skill separately in Capability Policy; enabling Gmail does not require enabling Email / SMTP for Gmail sends. Setup does not enable either skill automatically.

App-password Gmail supports search, messages, threads, attachments, drafts, send/reply/forward, read/star/importance state, archive, trash/spam restoration, targeted permanent deletion, file import/export, and custom labels. Filters, account settings, categories, send-as identities, and label color/visibility require an OAuth account. System folders are protected. Reads use BODY.PEEK and preserve unread state. Gmail remains the mailbox authority; there is no background sync.

The socket timeout defaults to 30 seconds and can be changed in this profile (1–120 seconds). Each network operation has a total deadline of min(300, timeout_seconds × 4) seconds. These settings do not control model generation or thinking.

Draft replacement returns a new draft reference after creating and verifying the replacement. If retiring the original fails, the result reports partial completion and both references. Removal moves the exact draft to Trash. SMTP acceptance remains confirmed if subsequent draft cleanup fails; cleanup never resends. A lost write acknowledgment is an unknown effect and blocks automatic replay. An exact Sent-folder match can reconcile an uncertain send; an inconclusive search never authorizes another send. Gmail already saves SMTP-sent messages, so the integration never appends a second Sent copy.

Continuation tokens and bulk previews expire after ten minutes and on restart. Account edits or mailbox UIDVALIDITY changes invalidate them; request a fresh search/preview. Approved bulk operations use exactly the previewed IDs and report confirmed, failed and unattempted items.

App-password continuation tokens are consumed when used, including a continuation that later fails its mailbox-identity check. A fresh page supplies a new token when more results remain. Searches reject more than 50,000 unique results; narrow the query if gmail_search_too_large is returned. Full MIME reads share a 25-MiB budget within one Gateway operation, so a large thread can exceed the budget even when each individual message fits.

Connect with OAuth

Enable the Gmail skill in Capability Policy. In Parameter Store → New → Gmail OAuth App, enter your existing Google OAuth application's client ID and client secret. Save it as gmail_auth_app. smTO does not supply or register a Google OAuth application.

{
  "profile_type": "gmail_oauth_app",
  "profile_version": 1,
  "service": "gmail",
  "client_type": "desktop",
  "client_id": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
  "client_secret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
  "authorization_uri": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth",
  "token_uri": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token",
  "scopes": [
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.labels"
  ]
}

The template fills in Google's endpoints. Desktop clients use a temporary loopback callback and the system browser. Web clients require client_type: "web" and a redirect_uri registered with Google, pointing to your controller's /api/agent/gmail/oauth/callback. On a remote controller, use a web application callback reachable from your browser; the desktop callback runs on the controller machine.

Ask:

Connect Gmail using @gmail_auth_app and save the account as work_gmail.

gmail.connect opens Google consent or returns an authorization link. After consent, the callback creates a Gmail Account Parameter Store record named work_gmail. OAuth handshake state expires after ten minutes and is lost on restart; restart the connection if necessary. No mailbox synchronization runs after connection.

The account record contains email, the linked OAuth app reference, tokens, expiry, and granted scopes. The model receives account identity, never raw secrets. Token refresh is automatic and updates that same Parameter Store entry. A revoked refresh token returns reauthorization_required; reconnect to the same key using the same OAuth app and Google account. A different account cannot silently replace it.

Use Gmail

  • “Use @work_gmail and summarize unread mail from today.”
  • “Find the latest message from alice@example.com using @work_gmail.”
  • “Draft a reply in @work_gmail.”
  • “Send the reviewed Gmail draft.”
  • “Forward Susan's PDF from @work_gmail to John.”
  • “Trash promotions older than one year in @personal_gmail.”

The main agent chooses searches, reads relevant messages or threads, and writes summaries or replies. Gmail tools contain no separate planning or summarization model. Email bodies, headers and attachment filenames remain untrusted external data.

Search supports Gmail query syntax and concrete structured filters, returns metadata first, and exposes continuation tokens. Bodies are bounded and truncation is explicit. Attachment presence is unknown in metadata-only results; read the selected message for attachment details. Counts report a lower bound when their explicit maximum is reached.

Search pages contain at most 100 messages. Check failed_messages as well as next_page_token: a page can be incomplete because an individual message could not be read. Message bodies are limited to 20,000 characters by default. A REST thread read keeps the last 100 messages, up to 40,000 body characters across them, and at most 100 attachment entries. App-password thread reads reject threads larger than 100 messages before fetching their bodies; use search and explicit message reads for a larger thread. A truncated result is not a complete mailbox or conversation export; use a narrower selection or the file-export tools when appropriate.

Drafts, labels, filters, and sends operate directly in Gmail. Compose and reply support text, HTML, CC/BCC, and attachments. For outgoing attachments, pass an existing artifact:// reference, a granted uploaded ctx_... / context:// reference, an artifact-workspace:// path, or a file supported by the normal task temporary-file publication mechanism. Explicit downloads become normal run artifacts; Gmail has no attachment cache. Forwarding can include the original message and attachments.

Filter operations need https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic. Add that scope to the OAuth app and reconnect explicitly. Tools report missing scope without widening authorization automatically.

Client actions and supported connections

One Gmail skill exposes client actions in discovery sections. The initial tools include gmail.capabilities, gmail.mark_all_read, and gmail.empty_trash. The model selects an action and supplies arguments; selection, batching and verification run in code without model calls between batches. This adds agent capabilities, not a separate email-client UI.

Use gmail.capabilities(account_ref="@work_gmail") to inspect the selected account's available actions, missing OAuth scopes, Gateway version and protocol requirements. This is a live capability check for app-password accounts; saving an account remains local.

Area Tools and behavior OAuth App password / Gateway
Inspection mailbox_overview, search, search_threads, count, read_message, read_thread, read_headers Yes Yes
Read status mark_all_read, mark_read, mark_unread Yes Yes
Priority star, unstar, mark_important, mark_not_important Yes Yes
Organization archive, move_to_inbox, move_to_label, apply_labels, remove_labels Yes Yes
Categories set_category for Personal, Social, Promotions, Updates or Forums Yes Unavailable
Cleanup trash, restore_to_inbox, mark_spam, mark_not_spam Yes MOVE required when changing folders
Permanent deletion delete_permanently, empty_trash, empty_spam Full https://mail.google.com/ scope UIDPLUS; MOVE when selected mail is outside Trash
Composition Existing compose, reply, reply-all, forward, draft edit/send/discard; reply_and_archive Yes Yes, using SMTP for sends
Forward as attachment send_forward / create_forward_draft with as_attachment=true Yes Yes
Send-as identity Existing compose/reply/forward tools with send_as Existing verified identity only Unavailable
Files list_attachments, download_attachment, download_attachments, export_messages, import_message Yes Yes; import requires UIDPLUS
Labels labels, get_label, create_label, update_label, delete_label Yes, including color and visibility List, counts, create, rename, delete
Rules Existing filter CRUD, replace_filter, apply_filter, create_filter_and_apply Yes, subject to settings scopes Unavailable
Settings get_settings / update_settings: vacation, language, POP, IMAP, primary identity Yes, subject to settings scopes Unavailable
Existing identities and forwarding list_send_as, get_forwarding Read only Unavailable

All tool IDs above have the gmail. prefix. Existing primitive IDs remain supported. Search accepts Gmail query syntax or structured filters. Reads are bounded and report truncation. get_label returns actual label counts; mailbox_overview includes up to 100 label count records and a separately bounded unread count. IMAP exposes message counts, not invented thread totals. Deleting a custom label leaves its messages intact.

Native snooze, scheduled send, Undo Send, mute/unmute, blocking, subscription management, and confidential mode are explicitly unavailable. There is no browser fallback, substitute filter, or local schedule claiming to be a native Gmail feature. Creating/deleting aliases, changing another send-as identity, and changing forwarding settings are unavailable for current account types. Contacts, Calendar, security and Workspace administration belong outside this skill; domain-delegated service-account authentication is not added here.

Compound mailbox changes

For “mark all unread mail as read,” use one call:

{"account_ref":"@work_gmail"}

Pass those arguments to gmail.mark_all_read. To restrict it to the Inbox, add "scope":"inbox". Normal all_mail is the default and excludes Spam and Trash. The cleanup helpers empty_trash and empty_spam always select their named folder; emptying means permanent deletion, not moving messages into Trash.

Other actions require exactly one selector: query, message_ids, or thread_ids. An empty query means all messages within the explicit scope. Supported scopes are all_mail, inbox, trash, spam, and anywhere. Explicit IDs must agree with the scope; selected threads expand to their existing message IDs before any write. For example:

{"account_ref":"@work_gmail","query":"older_than:1y","scope":"inbox"}

Pass this to gmail.archive. move_to_label also requires labels containing one user label ID or exact name. It adds that label and removes Inbox, preserving other labels. apply_labels and remove_labels accept multiple user labels.

The workflow collects a frozen selection and required state before mutation. Ordinary state changes never fetch message headers or bodies. Approval, when policy requires it, shows account, action, scope, count and permanent-deletion semantics. The model never carries selection tokens between these steps. Prepared selections expire after ten minutes, on controller restart or account changes; IMAP writes also validate UIDVALIDITY and Gmail message identity. An invalid approved selection cannot silently become a new selection.

The selection ceiling is 50,000 messages (max_messages can lower it). If more match, the action stops before mutation with an explicit limit result. It does not process a subset as “all,” repeatedly rerun a changing query, or include later arrivals.

Results contain selected, changed, unchanged, failed, unknown, and unattempted counts, completion/verification state, an operation reference and bounded error details. changed counts acknowledged updates; verification checks the selected IDs' intended state or disappearance. Remaining matching mail is a separate observation, so a new unread arrival does not invalidate a successfully completed initial selection. Activity shows selection, updating and verification progress without intermediate model turns.

OAuth label updates use native batches of up to 1,000 IDs; permanent deletion uses messages.batchDelete. Independent operations such as Trash requests use HTTP multipart batches of at most 50 with per-item receipts. These have different failure handling. App-password updates group UID flags, labels and moves in batches of up to 500 IDs, using one IMAP connection per batch and retaining selection mappings. Permanent deletion moves only selected messages to Trash when necessary, sets Deleted only on their exact UIDs, and uses targeted UID EXPUNGE. Unrestricted EXPUNGE and expunging CLOSE are never used; other clients' pending deletions remain untouched. Account-wide deletion settings are never changed implicitly.

Selection and state verification still require provider traffic. IMAP can be slower than OAuth and remains subject to mailbox size, server latency and deadlines; batching removes per-message logins and mutations, not those protocol costs. New guidance changes future tool choices and does not redirect an already-running header search.

The legacy preview_modify → batch_modify → count workflow remains available. A preview token covers its full selection; sampled IDs do not. displayed_ids_truncated limits the display, while truncated means the selection is incomplete. Keep account, operation and label name unchanged when executing its token. For legacy count verification use the same query and explicit label_ids: omission means Inbox; [] means normal All Mail. Prefer a named compound action for common tasks.

Do not treat an incomplete legacy preview as “all matching mail”: its token can still execute the selected subset. The controller keeps at most 100 active selections, shared between legacy previews and compound-action approval snapshots. Once execution consumes a valid token, a later label error or provider failure does not make it reusable. Inspect the outcome before preparing any new mutation.

Composition, files, rules and settings

reply_and_archive freezes the existing thread selection, sends the reply, persists the send receipt, then archives that selection. Archiving failure never resends the reply. send_as must name an existing verified OAuth identity; the primary account still owns thread identity and reply-all recipient exclusion. Forward-as-attachment emits a real message/rfc822 attachment.

export_messages accepts a normal selection and format="zip" (default) or "eml". Individual .eml exports and attachment downloads are limited to 100 files; total source content is limited to 25 MiB per invocation. ZIP entries use generated safe names. Downloads and exports become existing run artifacts; only references and metadata enter model context. import_message accepts file_ref for a valid .eml artifact/upload through the normal artifact-access mechanism. Import is a write and an uncertain import is never replayed.

replace_filter creates the replacement first, persists its ID, then deletes the old filter. A cleanup failure reports both IDs. apply_filter takes an existing filter ID; create_filter_and_apply takes criteria and action. Retroactive application validates queryable criteria and equivalent mailbox label effects before changes. It rejects forwarding and delivery-time-only settings rather than pretending to apply them to old mail.

Settings use a setting of vacation, language, pop, imap, or primary_identity. Updates supply values with only supported fields; omitted fields are preserved. Primary identity updates permit signature, display name and reply-to address. Changing an IMAP deletion setting is possible only through an explicit settings update, never as an internal delete workaround. Settings writes need gmail.settings.basic; additional mail operations need their own granted scopes. Capabilities report the exact requirements without upgrading authorization automatically.

Provider contracts: native batch modification, HTTP batching, permanent deletion scope, targeted UID expunging, alias restrictions, forwarding restrictions.

Accounts, confirmation, and reliability

Multiple accounts are separately named parameters: @work_gmail, @personal_gmail, or any chosen key. Rename an account through the normal Parameter Store editor and use the new @name immediately. Explicit tool references win; otherwise a single accepted Gmail reference or a single available account can supply the account. Multiple candidates require selection. Account operations resolve current Parameter Store authorization, so deletion or rename takes effect immediately. If renaming an OAuth app, update the accounts' oauth_app_ref as well.

Mutations use the existing permission and confirmation policy. gmail.preview_modify resolves a bounded exact selection and returns a ten-minute, one-use selection token. gmail.batch_modify executes those IDs after approval, without rerunning the query. A restart or expiry requires a new preview. OAuth label/state changes use native batches of at most 1,000 messages. Trash is reversible; permanent deletion is explicit and follows the same permission policy.

A lost write response may mean Gmail applied the operation. smTO reports an unknown effect and the runtime prevents automatic replay. Sends use RFC822 Message-ID reconciliation against Sent where possible; an inconclusive lookup never triggers another send.

Existing installations

Existing gmail_oauth_app and gmail_account Parameter Store records remain supported without migration. Startup does not import, rewrite, rename or remove old credential files. Reconnect explicitly if credentials are not already available in Parameter Store.

For a shared Google Workspace identity, use auth.google_connect with a google_oauth_app and the Gmail features needed. Existing gmail.* tools also accept the resulting google_account. They validate operation-specific granted scopes and return google.scope_upgrade_required on the selected account when access is missing. Use that same account key when adding Calendar or Drive features. See Shared Google Workspace identity.

OAuth configuration and authorization live in Parameter Store. There is no extra Gmail settings page, credential database, or primary-account database. Legacy sync, cache removal, broker callback, and OAuth configuration routes return HTTP 410. Parameter Store encryption and vault integration are separate future work.
